title: Which number does this digit riddle describe?
description: A riddle gives a number whose digits are all the tiniest odd digit, with the number of digits, the digit sum and the digital root all equal to the largest odd single digit. Each clue becomes one fact about the digits, and a check confirms all three. Keeko's doubt is that the tiniest odd digit is zero.
teaching_notes: One idea: turn each clue of a riddle into one fact about the digits, then check every clue. Watch for students who call zero the tiniest odd digit, or who forget that the digit count is also a clue.

source: Solve the riddle: digits each the tiniest odd digit, with the digit count, digit sum and digital root all equal to the largest odd single digit
video_script.why: A learner turns each clue of a digit riddle into one fact about the digits and checks all the clues together.
video_script.substitution: the book's own riddle about the tiniest and the largest odd digit
video_script.anchor: a riddle card with three clues and empty digit boxes
video_script.wrong_answer: the tiniest odd digit is zero
video_script.wrong_move: takes zero as the tiniest odd digit
video_script.payoff_line: The number is nine ones, eleven crore eleven lakh eleven thousand one hundred eleven.

final_answer.spoken: the number is nine ones, eleven crore eleven lakh eleven thousand one hundred eleven

maths_rules: the odd digits are 1, 3, 5, 7, 9; the tiniest is 1, so every digit is 1
the largest odd single digit is 9, so the number has 9 digits
nine 1s have digit sum 9, and the digital root of 9 is 9
111111111 has 9 digits, digit sum 9 and digital root 9; in words, eleven crore eleven lakh eleven thousand one hundred eleven
0 splits into two equal groups with nothing left, so 0 is even, not odd
video_script.design: One idea: turn each clue into one fact about the digits, then check all of them. Assumes the digital root and the digit sum. The riddle card stays on the board all video.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a riddle from your book about a number.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Every digit is the tiniest odd digit.
<bookmark mark='clue'/>The number of digits, the digit sum and the digital root are each the largest odd single digit.
Which number is it?

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

narration: <bookmark mark='digits'/>A single digit is one of zero, one, two, and so on up to nine.
<bookmark mark='share'/>An odd digit leaves one over when shared into two equal groups. An even digit leaves none.

beats.on_screen: Given: every digit is the tiniest odd digit; digit count, digit sum and digital root are each the largest odd single digit
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, every digit is the tiniest odd digit. The digit count, digit sum and digital root are each the largest odd single digit.

marks.find: the question is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the number.

beats.on_screen: The odd digits are 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. The tiniest is 1, so every digit is 1

marks.one: 1 is circled and every digit box is marked 1

narration: <bookmark mark='odd'/>Step one, the odd digits are one, three, five, seven and nine.
<bookmark mark='one'/>The tiniest is one, so every digit of the number is one.

beats.on_screen: The largest odd single digit is 9, so the number has 9 digits

marks.nine: 9 is circled in the row of odd digits

narration: <bookmark mark='nine'/>Step two, the largest odd single digit is nine.
<bookmark mark='boxes'/>The number of digits is nine too, so we have nine ones.

beats.on_screen: Nine ones: 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 9. A digit sum of 9 is a single digit, so the digital root is 9
narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>Step three, nine ones add to nine, so the digit sum is nine.
<bookmark mark='root'/>Nine is a single digit, so the digital root is nine too.

beats.on_screen: Check: 9 digits, digit sum 9, digital root 9, every digit 1
narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step four, check every clue. The number has nine digits, and each digit is one.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>The digit sum is nine.
<bookmark mark='root'/>The digital root is nine. All the clues hold.

marks.ans: the nine ones are written in the boxes

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The number is nine ones, eleven crore eleven lakh eleven thousand one hundred eleven.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the tiniest odd digit is zero.
<bookmark mark='even'/>But zero shares into two equal groups with nothing left over, so zero is even.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The tiniest odd digit is one.
